installation.note: systemctl is built-in on modern Linux distributions using systemd (Ubuntu 15.04+, Debian 8+, etc.)

overview.summary: systemctl controls systemd, the system and service manager on modern Linux systems. It manages system services (start, stop, restart, enable, disable), checks service status, and controls system state. Essential for managing services, daemons, and system operations on systemd-based systems.

misconceptions.title: systemctl works on all Linux systems
misconceptions.reality: systemctl is for systemd-based systems (Ubuntu 15.04+, Debian 8+, RHEL 7+). Older systems use init.d or Upstart. Check if systemd is used first.
misconceptions.tip: systemctl is for systemd. Older systems use service command or /etc/init.d scripts. Check: systemctl --version to see if available.

misconceptions.title: systemctl status requires sudo
misconceptions.reality: systemctl status doesn't need sudo - you can check status without privileges. Only start/stop/enable/disable need sudo.
misconceptions.tip: systemctl status works without sudo. Only control commands (start, stop, enable) need sudo.

common_pitfalls.solution: Use sudo for control commands (start, stop, restart, enable, disable). Status doesn't need sudo.
Check service name: systemctl list-units --type=service. Service names usually don't include .service extension in commands.

related_commands.relationship: Service management; service is older command, systemctl is modern
related_commands.description: Manage services (older systems, or wrapper for systemctl)

related_commands.relationship: Service logs; systemctl manages services, journalctl shows logs

best_practices: Use systemctl status to check service state
Use sudo for control commands (start, stop, enable, disable)
Use systemctl enable to make services start on boot
Use systemctl restart after configuration changes
Check service logs with journalctl -u service-name
Verify service started: systemctl is-active service-name

additional_notes.systemd_only: systemctl is for systemd-based systems (Ubuntu 15.04+, modern Linux). Older systems use different init systems.
additional_notes.common_commands: Most common: systemctl status (check), systemctl start/stop/restart (control), systemctl enable/disable (boot)
additional_notes.service_names: Service names usually don't include .service extension: systemctl start nginx (not nginx.service)
additional_notes.sudo_required: Control commands need sudo: start, stop, restart, enable, disable. Status doesn't need sudo.
